text:
# Power station and solar combo for an RV

The pages I read gave specs but almost no prices or panel model names. Treat the picks below as starting points and check current prices before you buy.

## Pick by how you camp

| RV use | Power station | Why | Solar |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Weekend trips, fridge, lights, laptops, CPAP** | Jackery Explorer 1000-class with a SolarSaga panel | AcquiredSense calls this the sweet spot for camping and road trips. | One Jackery SolarSaga panel. The page gave no wattage. |
| **Full-time or long boondocking, roof AC or induction cooking** | EcoFlow DELTA Pro 3 (4,096 Wh, 4,000 W continuous, 8,000 W surge) | It has the most capacity and output of the five units EmergencyEnergy compared. It expands past 12 kWh and is quiet at low load. | 300–400 W or more of folding panels, which is the article's rule for mid-size stations. |
| **Heavy solar charging** | Jackery Explorer 3000 Pro (3,024 Wh, 3,000 W) | The article cites solar input up to about 1,400 W. It runs a 300 W load for about 8.5 hours. | Large panel array to use that input. |
| **Mid-size, good value** | BLUETTI AC200L (2,048 Wh, 2,400 W) | It accepts a folding solar array directly. It runs about 50 dBA at full load, so it's louder. | 300–400 W folding array. |
| **Budget big capacity** | ALLPOWERS R4000 (3,456 Wh, 3,600 W continuous, 6,000 W peak) | It takes up to 2,000 W of solar input and has a 5-year warranty. It weighs 45 kg (about 99 lb), so it's better left in place than carried. | Up to 2,000 W of panels across three inputs. |

## My suggestion
- **Most RVers:** The EcoFlow DELTA Pro 3 plus 400 W or more of panels is the strongest all-around setup. It's the one with room to grow.
- **Lowest cost for a large battery:** The ALLPOWERS R4000 is $1,499 at the store price. Code EXTRA12 takes it to **$1,319.12**. It expires 2026-11-15, and one code per order is typical. [Buy the ALLPOWERS R4000](https://dealectric.com/go/allpowers-r4000-3456wh). This is an affiliate link, so Dealectric earns a commission at no cost to you. Sale items may not be returnable, even though there's a 30-day return window for unused items.

## Caveats
- **Roof AC:** A 13,500 BTU unit usually needs about 1,500 W or more when running, plus a startup surge. Even 3–4 kWh stations will run it for only about 2 hours (the article's figures are 1.7 hours for the Jackery 3000 Pro and 2.3 hours for the DELTA Pro 3). If you want AC, you'll need an expandable battery.
- **Panels:** I couldn't verify specific panel models or prices from these sources. The EcoFlow, Jackery and Bluetti sites sell matching folding panels.
- **Sources:** AcquiredSense listed only generic affiliate links and no specs. EmergencyEnergy gave no prices, and its links go to Amazon searches. Both are thin on detail.

Tell me your main loads (roof AC, fridge, microwave) and how many days off-grid you want, and I can narrow this to one setup.

Sources: [AcquiredSense](https://www.acquiredsense.com/reviews/power-stations.html), [EmergencyEnergy](https://www.emergencyenergy.co/articles/rv-power-station/), [Dealectric ALLPOWERS R4000](https://dealectric.com/lab/V4/allpowers-r4000-3456wh)
